newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada building permits fall 8.9 pct in August.
newsitem.headline: Canada building permits fall 8.9 pct in August.

text.p: The value of Canadian building permits issued in August fell 8.9 percent to C$2.19 billion, seasonally adjusted, from July, Statistics Canada said on Friday.
Aug Month pct chg Yr pct change
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast on average a month-on-month rise of 2.3 percent after June's 7.1 percent rise.
Statistics Canada said that the sharp fall in housing intentions followed three straight months of robust growth.
"Despite this setback, better affordability, recent buoyant house sales and the highest level of confidence since 1994...all point to further growth in the housing sector in the short term," it said.
The value of residential building permits over the first eight months of 1996 was up 14.1 percent from the same period in 1995.

"According to its latest revised prediction, Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation expects housing starts to rise 11 percent in 1996 to better reflect year-to-date residential permit results," Statistics Canada said.
"This suggests further growth in construction employment."
It said recent drops in mortgage rates also held promise for further improvement in the housing sector.
The drop in non-residential building permits was due entirely to a 44.5 percent plunge in the institutional component, overcoming 8.5 percent industrial and 0.1 percent commercial rises.
Building permits are an early indicator of future demand for labor and material by construction and contruction-related industries.
According to the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, about 95 percent of the residential building permits issued translate into actual housing starts.
